subject: Ceres-XL service anomalies — interim customer briefing and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@acme-commerce.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Ceres-XL: elevated server errors impacting some generation requests

Hi Nora —

Thanks for flagging the intermittent failures you saw this morning. We’ve identified an elevated rate of 5xx / generation timeouts affecting Ceres-XL on a subset of requests: mainly long-context multimodal prompts and requests with very high prompt token counts (>12k).

Immediate actions we’ve taken:
- Redirected a portion of Acme traffic to a compatible fallback model (Ceres-XL-v2) to reduce user-facing errors.
- Toggled a conservative batching cap for your tenant to lower cross-request contention.
- Captured trace-level logs for the affected request IDs you provided and uploaded a sample to the shared incident page (link below).

We don’t yet have a completed root cause but preliminary signals point to a KV-cache eviction pathology in the quantized kernel path that gets triggered under heavy long-sequence workloads. Our infra team is prioritizing kernel-level tracing now.

What you should expect in the next hour: we’ll continue routing traffic to the fallback model, watch for error-rate regression, and share a short customer-facing note once we confirm the rollout is holding.

Attachments: ceres_error_sample.log (short trace excerpt)
Links: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/CERES-20280530

Alex Martinez
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

---

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-30T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ceres-XL: elevated server errors impacting some generation requests

Alex / team —

Quick update from infra triage: we reproduced the high 5xx rate locally by replaying long-seq multimodal sessions against the quantized execution path. Root cause hypothesis refined: a race during KV cache resize causes stale pointers that only manifest when multiple streams share a device under the new continuous-batching changes we shipped last month.

Mitigations applied (11:00 PDT):
- Hotfix: add a lightweight KV-resize lock for the quantized kernels in affected runtime builds (deployed to canary).
- Traffic policy: all Acme traffic pinned to Ceres-XL-v2 and a hard token-limit of 8k for pending requests.
- Fallback policy: automatically reroute requests that exceed token limits to an unquantized variant to avoid cache paths.

We’re seeing error-rate drop on canary and the customer-routed traffic is trending down after reroute. Still validating stability under load tests; ETA for broader rollout if stable: ~4 hours.

Planned follow-ups for postmortem: collect reproducer prompts, kernel traces, and a timeline of when continuous-batching changes touched the quantized path. Marissa — can you own customer comms and confirm the message tone?

Dylan
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@acme-commerce.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-30T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ceres-XL: elevated server errors impacting some generation requests — summary & next steps

Nora —

Thanks again for the quick signal and for validating the improvement. Below is a short summary you can share with leadership, plus next steps and what we’ll include in the postmortem.

Summary (short):
Redwood observed elevated 5xx/timeouts on the Ceres-XL model for long-context multimodal requests in the 2028-05-30 08:50–11:20 PDT window. The issue was triggered by a race condition in the quantized kernel’s KV-cache resize path when under continuous-batching pressure. Mitigations: immediate traffic reroute to Ceres-XL-v2, a soft token cap (8k), and a kernel-level hotfix applied to canary that prevents concurrent resize races. Customer-facing error rates have reduced to near baseline following these actions.

Permanent fix ETA: The kernel patch is targeted for full rollout within 24–36 hours pending final load validation. No client-side changes are required.

Data retention: logs and traces for the incident window will be retained and available to Acme for 90 days; we will publish the trace archive link to the incident page by EOD.

Postmortem plan (what we’ll produce):
- Timeline of detections and actions
- Root cause analysis with kernel trace excerpts
- Reproducer prompts and a minimal test harness for your QA team
- Remediation plan (code + infra changes) and verification steps
- Compensation / SLA credit request process if required (we’ll surface options in the postmortem)

Action items:
- Marissa: draft a customer-facing postmortem and share for review by 2028-05-31 10:00 PDT.
- Dylan: finish kernel trace annotations and verify full rollout on staging; target complete in 24–36 hours.
- Stephanie: prepare a short internal runbook for future similar degradations (KV-cache instrumentation + rollback steps).

We’ll keep the incident page up to date (https://status.redwood.ai/incident/CERES-20280530). If you’d like that 30m bridge, we can stand one up at 16:30 PDT today.

Alex Martinez
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
